Version History: 2024.02.22 / 2024.03.28 / 2024.07.08

The 4-Wheel Differential Drive mode is the most common entry-level robot chassis structure. It controls 4 independent motors to drive each wheel individually, allowing zero-radius pivot turning by spinning left and right wheels at different speeds or in opposite directions.

Note: Since all 4 wheels are fixed in orientation, turning generates tire friction against the ground.

💡
Lock Screw Status: Direction Lock Screw must be FULLY TIGHTENED in Differential mode.

Mimicking real automotive steering geometry, the Ackermann configuration controls front-wheel steering angles via a dedicated servo motor. This setup provides superior stability during high-speed movement and precise cornering control.

It is widely adopted in National University Student Smart Car Competitions and autonomous driving research labs.

💡
Lock Screw Status: Direction Lock Screw must NOT BE INSTALLED in Ackermann mode to allow steering linkage motion.

Mecanum wheel drive enables full omnidirectional mobility—allowing the robot to move sideways (crab walk), diagonally, and spin in place. It is extensively used in robotics competitions like Robocon and FRC due to its extreme maneuverability.

Note: Requires relatively flat surfaces to maintain roller contact and traction.

💡
Lock Screw Status: Direction Lock Screw must be FULLY TIGHTENED in Mecanum mode.

steps.title: Acrylic Robotic Arm Packing List
steps.caption: Page 8: Packing List - Acrylic Robotic Arm Kit

blocks.html: Kit Components: Precision acrylic arm linkages, claw components, servos, brass standoffs, screws, and nylon lock nuts.

⚠️
1. Acrylic Fragility: Acrylic parts are brittle. Handle with care during assembly to avoid cracking.

2. Locknut Friction Rule: DO NOT overtighten nylon locknuts on revolving arm joints! Joints must swing smoothly. Overtightening increases servo resistance and will burn out / short-circuit the servo motor!

3. Servo Neutral Calibration: Do NOT rotate servo horns manually before installation. Power on the servo to let it return to its neutral 90° position before securing servo arms.

steps.title: Screw Model Identification & Parts Reference Guide
steps.caption: Page 11: Hardware & Screw Identification Guide

blocks.html: Most fasteners in this kit are standard GB cross-head (Phillips) screws, primarily categorized into M2 (Black) and M2.5 (Silver).

steps.title: Steering Module: Tie Rod & Motor Seats
steps.caption: Page 12-13: Steering Module Sub-assembly

blocks.html:
Step 1.1: Connect the steering tie rod to the motor pressing plate.

Step 1.2: Install N20 gear motors into the motor mounting seats.

💡
Alignment Tip: Ensure the N20 motor gearbox is completely flush with the edge of the motor mounting seat.

Step 1.3: Connect the steering pressing plate to the motor seat using M2.5*10 silver self-tapping screws.

Step 2.2: Secure the motor pressing plate with N20 motors using M2.5*6 black self-tapping screws.

Step 2.3 - 2.4: Fit SG90 servo into the chassis slot and secure with M2.5*6 black self-tapping screws.

Step 2.5: Mount single-arm servo horn pointing vertically upward (90°). Fasten with M2*4 screw (silver, inside servo accessory bag).

Step 2.6: Place the assembled steering module into the main frame.

⚠️
Servo Re-centering Note: If the servo arm output shaft was manually rotated, re-center it electronically to neutral position before attaching the horn.

Step 2.7: Fix the steering module using M2.5*6 flat head silver self-tapping screws.

Step 2.8: Connect the servo arm to the steering linkage using M2*8 screw with washer (from servo bag).

💡
Hole Location: Fasten screw into the 2nd hole of the servo arm. Apply firm force to drive the thread in.

Step 2.9: Push the 4 wheels onto the N20 motor output D-shafts.

Step 2.10: Insert side baffles into the chassis frame slots.

💡
D-Shaft Alignment: Align the flat face of the motor shaft with the flat side of the wheel center hole before inserting.

steps.title: Direction Lock Screw Configuration per Mode
steps.caption: Page 23: Direction Lock Screw Setup Rules

blocks.html: Thread M2.5*6 black self-tapping screw into the direction lock hole according to your desired chassis mode:

🚨
CRITICAL WARNING: When the direction lock screw is fully tightened, DO NOT programmatically drive the steering servo, or gear stripping and servo burnout will occur!

Step 3.1: Fix ABS side plates to the acrylic top plate using M2.5*6 black self-tapping screws.

Step 3.2: Mount the assembled acrylic upper deck onto the lower chassis using M2.5*6 black self-tapping screws.

Step 3.3: Install front and rear top plates using M2.5*6 black self-tapping screws.
Select the standoff configuration matching your controller board:

3.4.1 / 3.5.1: Thread single-head brass standoffs M2.5*7+6 into designated top plate grid holes and secure with M2.5 nuts.
3.4.2 / 3.5.2: Align mainboard mounting holes onto standoffs and secure with M2.5*6 silver screws.

steps.title: Mecanum Coupler & Roller Orientation Setup
steps.caption: Page 34-35: Mecanum Wheel Coupler & Direction Setup

blocks.html:
Step 2.1.0 (Coupler): Slide metal coupler onto N20 motor shaft. Align coupler side set screw with motor D-shaft flat side and tighten securely. Fasten wheel using M2.5*8 screw x1 per wheel.

Mecanum Roller Orientation Rule: Mecanum wheels are split into Left-handed (L) and Right-handed (R) roller directions.

💡
Top View Pattern Rule: When viewed from above, the rollers on top of the 4 wheels must form an "X" shape pointing towards the center of the chassis.

steps.title: Arm Base Assembly & Servo Initial Neutral Position
steps.caption: Page 36-37: Arm Base & Servo Neutral Position

blocks.html:
Step 3.1.0: Assemble base structural acrylic plates using M2.5*8 screws x2 and M2.5 nuts x2. Pay close attention to servo orientation.

Step 3.1.7 (Servo Horn Neutral): Mount single-arm servo horn in default vertically upward (90°) position.

⚠️
Neutral Calibration Rule: Do NOT rotate servo arm manually before installation. If rotated, power on servo to return to mid-point (90°) before mounting horn. Fasten with M1.6*5 black screw or shortest servo screw.

steps.title: Main Arm Acrylic Linkages & Servo Horn Fixation
steps.caption: Page 38-39: Main Arm Linkage & Servo Fastening

blocks.html:
Step 3.1.12: Attach small acrylic linkage to servo horn using M1.6*5 black self-tapping screws x2.

Step 3.1.13 - 3.1.14: Verify initial arm state: servo horn vertical, main upper arm in free state. Fasten horn to servo output gear using the shortest screw inside servo bag.

steps.title: Arm Standoffs & Joint Lock Nut Adjustment
steps.caption: Page 40-41: Arm Frame Standoffs & Joint Lock Nuts

blocks.html:
Step 3.1.18: Install 22mm brass standoffs (longest 22mm standoffs) using M2.5*8 screws x4 and M2.5 nuts x2.

Step 3.1.20: Install 15mm brass standoffs using M2.5*8 screws x4.

Step 3.1.22 - 3.1.27 (Joint Linkages): Connect side linkages using M2.5*12 and M2.5*10 screws with Nylon Lock Nuts.

🚨
DO NOT OVERTIGHTEN LOCK NUTS: Nylon lock nuts must be left slightly loose so joint linkages pivot freely. Overtightening restricts arm movement and causes servo short-circuit / failure!

Step 3.2.1 - 3.2.6: Assemble claw frame using M2.5*7+6 brass standoffs x2 and M2.5*6 screws x2. Secure claw servo with M2.5 nuts x2.

Step 3.2.7: Align claw servo horn per diagram angle and secure with longest screw from servo package bag.

Step 3.2.9 - 3.2.12: Assemble claw scissor linkages using M2.5*10 and M2.5*12 screws with Nylon Lock Nuts. Keep all pivot pins loose for low friction.

Step 3.2.15: Connect the claw assembly to the main arm body using M2.5*8 screws x3 and M2.5 nuts x3.

Step 3.2.23: Install the long actuation linkage rod using M2.5*10 screw x1 and Lock Nuts x2.

⚠️
FRAGILE PART NOTICE: The linkage connector in Step 3.2.15 is fragile! Do NOT apply excessive force during insertion. Use spare parts included in kit if broken.
